title: ProvisioningRequest
description: HTTP request body sent by a station to the server's provisioning endpoint (POST /api/v1/stations/provision) per Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2. Carries the single-use provisioning token that authorises issuance, the station's descriptive fields, and every public key the station asks the server to bind to its provisioned identity. The distinction between the two groups is normative: descriptive drift on a retry MUST be ignored, whereas a retry is a replay only if it presents the same set of key kinds, each carrying the same key, as the provision the token bound — the BOUND SET. A different key for a bound kind, or a different set of key kinds in either direction, MUST be rejected (Flows §2 — Single-use and idempotent retry). The server's response is defined by provisioning-response.schema.json.

provisioningToken.description: Single-use provisioning token authorising exactly one certificate issuance, with a TTL fixed at issuance (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2). Treated as an OPAQUE bearer credential: the station MUST NOT parse or derive meaning from its content. NOTE: §2's narrative step 2 describes the token as a UUID, but no normative statement pins its format, and deployed servers use other shapes (e.g. 64 hex characters); the constraint here is therefore a conservative opaque-string bound rather than a UUID pattern. Once consumed, superseded, or past its TTL the token is invalid for all purposes and the server rejects with 401 / 2019 PROVISIONING_TOKEN_INVALID.

serialNumber.description: Manufacturer serial number of the hardware serving this station. DESCRIPTIVE: it identifies the hardware, not the station (Chapter 01 — Architecture §2.1), and it MAY change across the station's life without changing the stationId. Drift in this field on a retry with the same token MUST be ignored. Matches the BootNotification serialNumber constraint.

bayCount.description: DEPRECATED (since 0.11.0, removed in 0.12.0): use bays instead, which declares the bay NUMBERS rather than only how many there are. A scalar count cannot express a non-dense bay set — a station with bays {1,3} declaring bayCount 2 asserts a bay 2 it does not have — and cannot carry the per-bay program list at all. Retained for one release so a station built against 0.10.0 still validates. When both are present bays is authoritative and bayCount MUST equal bays.length; a server MUST NOT derive topology from bayCount when bays is present. DESCRIPTIVE — drift on a retry MUST be ignored. Maximum bay count per controller is 64 (Chapter 01 — Architecture §4.2).

bays.description: The station's DECLARED PHYSICAL TOPOLOGY: the bays it has, and per bay the programs that bay can run. Declared here, at provisioning, because this is the moment the server creates the bay records the station will be addressed by. The station declares bay NUMBERS, not a count: the set need not be dense, so a station with bays {1,3} declares exactly those two and asserts nothing about a bay 2 (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2). A PROGRAM is a complete station-defined physical operation ('simple wash'), not a composable element ('brush', 'water'); it is identified within its bay by the ordinal programNumber. Programs are PHYSICAL and station-owned; SERVICES are commercial and server-minted, and the binding between them is created on the server by an operator and delivered to the station in the service catalog — the station never originates it (Chapter 01 — Architecture §4.2). Maximum 64 bays (Chapter 01 — Architecture §4.2): a real installation has 4-8, and 64 keeps the boot re-declaration far below the 64 KB MQTT Maximum Packet Size of Chapter 02 — Transport §1.2 even at the maximum programs per bay. A faulted bay or program is declared present-but-unavailable, never omitted: absence means the hardware itself changed and requires re-provisioning (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2).

bayNumber.description: The station-assigned ordinal identifying this bay physically. Unique within the request. The set of bayNumber values across bays need NOT be dense — {1,3} is a conforming declaration for a station whose bay 2 was never fitted.

programs.description: The programs this bay can run. Ordered by the station; order carries no meaning, programNumber does.

programNumber.description: The ordinal identifying this program within its bay. Unique within the bay; need NOT be dense. This is the value that travels in the service catalog and in StartService (Chapter 03 — Messages).

label.description: Human-readable name of the program, printable ASCII, unique within its bay. DESCRIPTIVE: it exists so an operator can tell which physical program is which when creating the service binding. It is declared here and is NOT compared at boot — a corrected typo in a firmware constant MUST NOT put a station into Pending (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2, descriptive drift). Drift in this field on a retry MUST be ignored, exactly as for serialNumber.

tlsCsr.description: PEM-encoded PKCS#10 Certificate Signing Request over the station's mTLS client key pair, generated on-device (the private key MUST NOT leave the station). ECDSA P-256; Subject CN MUST equal the stationId the token is bound to. The CSR's self-signature proves possession. IDENTITY-BEARING: on a retry, comparison is on the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, NOT the raw CSR bytes — ECDSA signatures are randomised, so two honest CSRs over the same key differ byte-wise and a byte comparison would reject a legitimate retry (Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2).

receiptSigningPublicKey.description: PEM-encoded ECDSA P-256 public key used by the server to verify offline transaction receipts (Chapter 06 — Security §6.2). Submitted as a BARE public key, not inside a CSR, and never certified. IDENTITY-BEARING — drift on a retry is rejected. It MUST be a DISTINCT key pair from the mTLS client key above: submitting the same public key as both is rejected with 422 / 4016 PROVISIONING_KEY_REUSE (Chapter 06 — Security §4.3), so that receipt verification survives rotation or revocation of the TLS credential. REQUIRED OF EVERY STATION, DELIBERATELY — including one that will never run an offline session. Its purpose is offline receipt verification, but it is collected at provisioning because that is the only moment the server can bind a key to this station's identity under a single-use token: the key set is frozen when the token is consumed, and a station that later gains offline capability cannot add a key without a new provisioning cycle. Requiring it unconditionally costs one secure-element slot and one keygen on a station that never uses it; making it conditional would cost a re-provision on every station that ever does. This is forward compatibility, not an offline dependency in the online path — nothing in the Core, Transaction or Security profiles reads this key.

stationPubKey.description: OPTIONAL. The station's dedicated static BLE ECDH P-256 public key (compressed SEC1, 44-char Base64), generated on-device, over which the server signs the StationIdentity certificate returned in the provisioning response (Chapter 06 — Security §6.5.2). Present ONLY for stations implementing the Offline/BLE profile; absent otherwise. Its presence is conditional on BLE support, which is declared in BootNotification (capabilities.bleSupported) and is therefore NOT expressible as a JSON Schema constraint on this request — the condition is prose-only, stated in Chapter 06 §6.5.2. IDENTITY-BEARING. On a retry the request is compared against the BOUND SET — the key kinds submitted at first provision and the key each carried — and is a replay only if it presents the same set of key kinds, each carrying the same key. Absence is exempt only when the key kind is absent on BOTH sides: a station that submitted no BLE key at first provision and submits none on retry is a replay, whereas omitting a BLE key that WAS bound, or adding one that was not, is drift and is rejected with 409 / 4015 PROVISIONING_KEY_MISMATCH. Chapter 04 — Protocol Flows §2 states the rule normatively. MUST be distinct from both ECDSA keys above (ECDSA-signing vs ECDH key-agreement key separation, NIST SP 800-56A); submitting it as either is rejected with 422 / 4016 PROVISIONING_KEY_REUSE, which covers all three pairwise collisions.
